minutes.headline: Board heard the Budget Task Force's 20 recommendations; foreclosure of 531 Reservoir Road and ARPA delegation approved.
minutes.summary: The board welcomed a new Council on Aging director, honored the outgoing one, and got a town manager search update with interviews planned for January 14 and 15. It heard the unaudited FY24 year-end financials and a long joint presentation from the Budget Task Force on revenue and savings ideas, including CPA and overrides. It voted on ambulance write-offs, license renewals, foreclosure of one tax-title parcel, and delegating remaining ARPA funds to the interim town manager.

public_comment.topic: Thanked the finance director, disagreed that Weston-style overrides are unaffordable, argued for larger annual tax increases, and said the superintendent should move students from IEPs to 504 plans; cut off after about five minutes.

Free cash came in higher than the earlier estimate because the finance director missed a line in the projection.
Quarter 1 uncollectible ambulance bills written off the books but still sent to collections.
Interim manager asked to boost the staff payroll line because there is no network administrator; ARPA and capital items reviewed.
Bids came in well above the budget left for the project.
Task force chair said inflation outpaced the levy limit, so real funding is falling.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted unanimously to authorize tax title foreclosure of 531 Reservoir Road and its eventual sale.
The board voted unanimously to entrust the remaining ARPA funds to the interim town manager, pending the school bid opening, with a report back.
The Budget Task Force gave a long joint presentation of recommendations on revenue and savings, including CPA and overrides; it was informational and no vote was taken.
The board heard the unaudited FY24 year-end financials, in which revenue came in above projection and free cash above the earlier estimate.
Town manager finalist interviews were set for January 14, with January 15 as backup, and the public may send candidate questions to the chair.

why_it_matters: The ARPA delegation means the last of the federal relief money can be committed by the interim town manager without a further board vote, with only a report back required.

The Budget Task Force's ideas on CPA and overrides are the kind of revenue options that would eventually reach residents as tax-bill changes or ballot questions, but nothing was decided at this meeting.
Foreclosure on the tax-title parcel moves it toward sale, and the choice of a permanent town manager will shape the next budget cycle.
watch_next: Town manager finalist interviews on January 14, with January 15 as backup.
The comparison communities list returning with an added wealth/affordability factor, followed by a formal vote.
